subject.name: Mathematics
subject.description: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics. Core students take Papers 1 and 3; Extended students take Papers 2 and 4. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

topics.title: Number
topics.summary: Types of number, fractions, decimals and percentages, standard form, bounds, ratio and proportion, compound interest.

topics.title: Algebra and graphs
topics.summary: Algebraic manipulation, equations and inequalities, sequences, functions, graphs and differentiation.

topics.title: Coordinate geometry
topics.summary: Gradients, midpoints, lengths of line segments and equations of straight lines.

topics.title: Geometry
topics.summary: Angle properties, similarity, symmetry and circle theorems.

topics.title: Mensuration
topics.summary: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume, arcs and sectors.

topics.title: Trigonometry
topics.summary: Pythagoras' theorem, right-angled trigonometry, sine and cosine rules, 3D problems.

topics.title: Transformations and vectors
topics.summary: Reflections, rotations, translations, enlargements and vector geometry.

topics.title: Probability
topics.summary: Probability of single and combined events, tree diagrams, conditional probability.

topics.title: Statistics
topics.summary: Averages and range, grouped data, cumulative frequency and histograms.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write 0.35 as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates did not simplify fully.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Work out {p}% of {n}.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Simplify 3a + 5b − a + 2b.
parts.examinerComment: Sign errors when collecting −a were common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve {a}x − {b} = {=a*x-b}.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line through ({x1}, {y1}) and ({=x1+d}, {=y1+m*d}).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates divided the change in x by the change in y.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Write down the y-intercept of the line y = {m}x − {c}.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are {a}° and {b}°. Find the third angle, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the sum of the interior angles of a polygon with {n} sides, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of a triangle with base {b} cm and perpendicular height {h} cm, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Forgetting the ½ was the most common error.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the volume of a cuboid measuring {a} cm by {b} cm by {c} cm, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides {=3*k} cm and {=4*k} cm. Find the length of the hypotenuse, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The bearing of B from A is {b}°. Find the bearing of A from B, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: A sketch with north lines at both points helps.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: The point (3, −2) is translated by the vector (−5, 4). Write down the coordinates of its image.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The point (4, 1) is reflected in the x-axis. Write down the coordinates of its image.
parts.examinerComment: Reflecting in the y-axis instead was a common error.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: The probability that it rains tomorrow is {p}. Find the probability that it does not rain.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A fair six-sided dice is thrown. Find the probability of getting a number greater than 4. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: 'Greater than 4' means 5 or 6, not 4, 5 or 6.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the mode of 3, 5, 5, 6, 8, 5, 2.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the range of 12, 7, {h}, {l}, 15.
parts.examinerComment: The range is a single value, not '4 to 19'.

questions.stem: The bar chart shows the number of pets owned by each of 30 students.

figures.alt: Bar chart of number of pets owned by 30 students: 0 pets 6, 1 pet 11, 2 pets 8, 3 pets 3, 4 pets 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write down the mode.
parts.examinerComment: The mode is the value with the highest frequency, not the frequency itself.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: How many students own 3 or more pets?
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the mean number of pets per student, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.examinerComment: Dividing by 5 (the number of bars) was a common error.

parts.prompt: Find the value of {=a^3}^(2/3).
parts.examinerComment: Find the root first, then the power.

parts.prompt: Expand and simplify (2x − 3)(x + 5).

markingPoints.text: M1 for 3 correct terms out of 2x², 10x, −3x, −15

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line with gradient −2 that passes through (0, 3). Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Find the exterior angle of a regular 12-sided polygon, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Find the volume of a sphere of radius {r} cm as a multiple of π. Enter the multiple only (for 10π enter 10).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Find the exact value of sin 30° + cos 60°.

markingPoints.text: B1 for sin 30° = ½ and cos 60° = ½

parts.examinerComment: Exact values should be learned.

parts.prompt: a = (2, −1) and b = (−3, 4) as column vectors. Find 3a − 2b, giving your answer as (x, y).
parts.examinerComment: Subtracting a negative component caused errors.

parts.prompt: P(A) = 1/3 and P(B) = 1/4. A and B are independent. Find P(A and B), as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: Some added the probabilities.

parts.prompt: From a cumulative frequency curve, the lower quartile is {q} and the upper quartile is {=q+d}. Find the interquartile range.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

figures.alt: Circle with centre O. A, B and C lie on the circle. Angle AOB at the centre is 110°. C is on the major arc. Not to scale.

parts.prompt: A, B and C are points on a circle, centre O. Angle AOB = 110°. Find angle ACB. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.

markingPoints.text: B1 for the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference

parts.examinerComment: The reason must use the correct theorem.

parts.prompt: Share ${=(2*a+d)*u} in the ratio {a} : {=a+d}. Find the larger share, in dollars.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Find the value of {a}x² − {c} when x = −{k}.
parts.examinerComment: Squaring after multiplying by the coefficient, i.e. ({a} × −{k})², is an order of operations error.

parts.prompt: Find the midpoint of (−2, 6) and (4, 0). Give your answer in the form (x, y).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: How many lines of symmetry does a regular hexagon have?
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Find the circumference of a circle of radius {r} cm, correct to 1 decimal place, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Using the diameter formula with the radius halved the answer.

parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle the hypotenuse is {h} cm and one angle is {t}°. Find the side opposite the {t}° angle, correct to 1 decimal place, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Labelling the sides before choosing sin, cos or tan helps.

parts.prompt: A shape is enlarged by scale factor {k}. One side is {s} cm long. Find the length of the corresponding side of the image, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: The probability that a spinner lands on red is {p}. It is spun {n} times. Find the expected number of times it lands on red.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Find the mean of 4.2, 5.6, 3.8 and 6.4.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

figures.alt: Right-angled triangle ABC with the right angle at B. AB = 5 cm, BC = 12 cm and AC = x cm. Not to scale.

parts.prompt: Triangle ABC is right-angled at B. Calculate x.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Amira invests ${P} in a savings account paying compound interest at a rate of {r}% per year. Calculate the value of the investment at the end of {n} years. Give your answer correct to the nearest cent.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates used the multiplier 1 + {r}/100 correctly. A common error was to calculate simple interest ({P} × {r}/100 × {n}) and add it to the principal, giving {=P+P*r*n/100}.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Amira invests ${P} in a savings account paying compound interest at a rate of {r}% per year. Find the smallest whole number of years after which the investment will first be worth more than ${=P*f}.

markingPoints.text: M1 for a trial such as {P} × (1 + {r}/100)^n, or a correct logarithmic method

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who showed their trials clearly usually earned the method mark. Some stopped one year too early without checking that the value exceeded ${=P*f}.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write 0.000 047 3 in standard form.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. Errors included 47.3 × 10^-6, which is not in standard form, and sign errors in the power.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The length of a rod is {L} cm, correct to the nearest millimetre. Write down the lower bound of the length.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates gave {=L-0.1} or {=L+0.05}. Remember the bounds are half a unit of accuracy either side of the stated value.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation {a}(x − {b}) = {c}x + {=a*(x-b)-c*x}.
parts.examinerComment: Generally well done. Weaker candidates expanded {a}(x − {b}) as {a}x − {b}.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Factorise completely 6x² − 15xy.

markingPoints.text: or B1 for a correct partial factorisation such as 3(2x² − 5xy) or x(6x − 15y)

parts.examinerComment: The word 'completely' signals that all common factors must be taken out. Many candidates removed only 3 or only x.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the nth term of the sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, …

markingPoints.text: or B1 for 4n + k (k ≠ 3) or jn + 3 (j ≠ 0)

parts.examinerComment: Common errors were n + 4 and 4n + 7, the latter from using the first term as the constant.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt:
Solve the simultaneous equations. Show all your working.
3x + 2y = 16
 x − 2y = 0

markingPoints.text: M1 for adding the equations to eliminate y (4x = 16) or a correct substitution

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who showed the elimination step clearly were most successful. Answers without working could only gain the accuracy marks if both values were correct.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A is the point ({x1}, {y1}) and B is the point ({=x1+dx}, {=y1-dy}). Find the gradient of the line AB.
parts.examinerComment: A frequent error was inverting the fraction (change in x over change in y). Sign errors were also common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A is the point ({x1}, {y1}) and B is the point ({=x1+dx}, {=y1-dy}). Find the length of AB.

markingPoints.text: M1 for square root of their sum

parts.examinerComment: Well answered by most. Some candidates added the coordinates instead of subtracting.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A is the point (2, 5) and B is the point (8, −3). Find the coordinates of the midpoint of AB. Give your answer in the form (x, y).

markingPoints.text: or B1 for one correct coordinate

parts.examinerComment: Very well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 156°. Find the number of sides of the polygon.
parts.examinerComment: Using the exterior angle is the most efficient method. Candidates using (n − 2) × 180 = 156n often made algebraic slips.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. Angle AOC = 128°. Find angle ABC, where B is on the major arc. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.

markingPoints.text: B1 for reason: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference

parts.examinerComment: Reasons must use correct geometrical language. 'Angle at centre is double' without reference to the circumference did not earn the mark.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Two similar bottles have heights {a} cm and {b} cm. The smaller bottle holds {v} ml. Calculate the volume the larger bottle holds, in ml.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates used the linear or area scale factor instead of cubing the length ratio for volume.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius {r} cm and angle {t}°. Calculate the arc length, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates calculated the sector area instead of the arc length.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A solid cylinder has radius {r} cm and height {h} cm. Calculate its total surface area, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: The most common error was to include only one circular end.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A cone has volume {v} cm³ and base radius {r} cm. Calculate the height of the cone, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who forgot the 1/3 obtained {=v/(pi*r^2)}.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: In triangle PQR, angle Q = 90°, PQ = {a} cm and QR = {b} cm. Calculate angle QPR, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Labelling the opposite and adjacent sides on a sketch helped candidates choose the correct ratio.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = {b} cm, AC = {c} cm and angle BAC = {A}°. Calculate the length of BC, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: A common error was evaluating ({b}² + {c}² − 2 × {b} × {c}) × cos {A}, which shows a misunderstanding of the order of operations.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: In triangle ABC, AB = {b} cm, AC = {c} cm and angle BAC = {A}°. Calculate the area of triangle ABC, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle T with vertices (1, 1), (3, 1), (1, 2) onto triangle U with vertices (−1, 1), (−1, 3), (−2, 1).
parts.examinerComment: Candidates must give a single transformation. Combinations of transformations scored zero. Many omitted the centre of rotation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: a = ({p}, −{q}) and b = ({r}, {s}) written as column vectors. Find |2a + b|, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found 2a + b correctly. Some then gave the vector rather than its magnitude.

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 red counters and 3 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that both counters are red. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates treated the selection as with replacement and gave 25/64.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the probability that the two counters are different colours. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who drew a tree diagram were more likely to consider both orders.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Given that at least one counter is red, find the probability that both are red. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: Conditional probability remains challenging. The condition reduces the sample space, so the denominator is P(at least one red).

questions.stem:
The masses, m kg, of 40 parcels are recorded.
0 < m ≤ 2: 6 parcels
2 < m ≤ 4: 14 parcels
4 < m ≤ 8: 12 parcels
8 < m ≤ 12: 8 parcels

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate an estimate of the mean mass, in kg.
parts.examinerComment: Common errors included using class widths or upper bounds instead of midpoints, and dividing by 4 (the number of classes).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: On a histogram, find the frequency density for the class 4 < m ≤ 8.
parts.examinerComment: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width. Some candidates divided by the upper class boundary.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Write down the modal class.
parts.examinerComment: With unequal class widths the modal class is the one with the highest frequency density. Here 2 < m ≤ 4 has density 7, the highest.

parts.prompt: Write 84 as a product of its prime factors.

markingPoints.text: M1 for a correct factor tree or repeated division, e.g. 84 = 2 × 42 = 2 × 2 × 21

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found the correct primes but listed them (2, 2, 3, 7) instead of writing a product. Some included 1 as a factor.

parts.prompt: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of {=4*g} and {=7*g}.

markingPoints.text: M1 for listing factors of both numbers or using prime factors

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates gave the lowest common multiple, {=28*g}, instead of the highest common factor.

parts.prompt: Work out 3/4 of {=4*k}.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. Dividing by 4 and then multiplying by 3 is the most efficient method.

parts.prompt: Write 5 600 000 in standard form.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates wrote 56 × 10⁵, which is not in standard form because 56 is not between 1 and 10.

parts.prompt: A map has a scale of 1 : {s}. A road is {d} cm long on the map. Find the real length of the road, in kilometres.

markingPoints.text: M1 for {d} × {s} (= {=d*s} cm) or a conversion of 1 cm to {=s/100000} km

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates multiplied correctly but many made errors converting centimetres to kilometres. There are 100 000 cm in 1 km.

parts.prompt: Expand 4(2x − 3).
parts.examinerComment: A common error was 8x − 3, multiplying only the first term in the bracket.

parts.prompt: Factorise completely 6y + 15.

markingPoints.text: or B1 for a correct partial factorisation with a common factor

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates identified 3 as the common factor. Check by expanding your answer.

parts.prompt: The nth term of a sequence is {a}n + {b}. Find term number {k} of the sequence.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. A few candidates substituted n = {=k+1} or found the first {k} terms one at a time, which is slow and error-prone.

parts.prompt: Solve x/{a} + {b} = {=m+b}.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates multiplied only the x term by {a}, forgetting to multiply the {b} as well, when they cleared the fraction first.

parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 3x + 2 < 17.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates solved correctly but then gave the answer as x = 5. The inequality sign must be kept.

parts.prompt: Write down the gradient of the line y = {c} − {m}x.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who rearranged mentally into the form y = mx + c rarely made errors. A common wrong answer was {c}.

parts.prompt: The point (p, {=m*p-c}) lies on the line y = {m}x − {c}. Find the value of p.
parts.examinerComment: Substituting the y-coordinate and solving the resulting equation was well done. Some candidates substituted {=m*p-c} for x instead of y.

parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point where the line y = 2x − 6 crosses the x-axis. Give your answer in the form (x, y).
parts.examinerComment: A common error was to give the y-intercept (0, −6). On the x-axis, y = 0.

parts.prompt: P is the point ({px}, 7). M is the midpoint of PQ and M is the point ({=px+d/2}, 4). Find the x-coordinate of Q.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ({px} + x)/2 = {=px+d/2} or a correct use of the change from P to M

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found the midpoint of P and M instead of using M as the midpoint of PQ.

parts.prompt: Four angles meet at a point. Three of the angles are {a}°, {b}° and {c}°. Find the fourth angle, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used 180° (angles on a straight line) instead of 360° (angles around a point).

parts.prompt: In an isosceles triangle, the angle between the two equal sides is {a}°. Find the size of one of the other two angles, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: A sketch marking the two equal angles helped candidates avoid giving {=180-2*a}, which comes from doubling the given angle.

parts.prompt: Lines AB and CD are parallel. A straight line crosses AB at P and CD at Q, with B and C on opposite sides of PQ. Angle BPQ = 64°. Find angle PQC. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.
parts.examinerComment: The reason must use the correct term. 'Z angles' is not accepted; 'alternate angles' is.

parts.prompt: Write down the order of rotational symmetry of a rhombus that is not a square.
parts.examinerComment: A common answer was 4, which is the order for a square.

parts.prompt: A trapezium has parallel sides of length {a} cm and {b} cm. The perpendicular distance between them is {h} cm. Find the area, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates multiplied all three lengths together. The formula is given on the formula sheet.

parts.prompt: A rectangle has area {=l*w} cm². Its length is {l} cm. Find its perimeter, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found the width correctly but then added only two sides.

parts.prompt: A cuboid measures {a} cm by {b} cm by {c} cm. Find its total surface area, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates calculated the volume, or included each face only once.

parts.prompt: Write down the bearing of a point that is due south-west of another point.
parts.examinerComment: Bearings are measured clockwise from north. Some candidates gave 135°, which is south-east.

parts.prompt: The point (4, 3) is reflected in the line x = 1. Write down the coordinates of its image.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who sketched the line x = 1 as a vertical line usually succeeded. Some reflected in the line y = 1.

parts.prompt: The point (3, 1) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Write down the coordinates of its image.
parts.examinerComment: Using tracing paper, or a sketch, helps. The anticlockwise answer (−1, 3) was a common error.

parts.prompt: a = (3, −1) and b = (2, 5) as column vectors. Find a + b, giving your answer as (x, y).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Triangle A has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (3, 2). Triangle B has vertices (4, −1), (6, −1) and (6, 0). Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.

markingPoints.text: B1 for vector (3, −2) written as a column vector

parts.examinerComment: The vector must be given as a column vector. Descriptions such as 'moved 3 right and 2 down' do not earn the second mark.

parts.prompt: The point (3, −1) is enlarged with scale factor 2 and centre (0, 0). Write down the coordinates of its image.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: A spinner can land on red, blue, green or yellow. P(red) = {a}, P(blue) = {b} and P(yellow) = {c}. Find P(green).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. The probabilities of all the possible outcomes add up to 1.

parts.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown and the scores are added. Find the probability that the total is 10. Give your answer as a fraction.

markingPoints.text: M1 for 3 favourable outcomes out of 36, e.g. (4, 6), (5, 5), (6, 4)

parts.examinerComment: A possibility diagram helps. Many candidates counted (4, 6) but not (6, 4), giving 2/36.

parts.prompt: The probability that a bus is late on any day is {p}, independently of other days. Find the probability that the bus is late on two particular days.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates added the probabilities, giving {=2*p}. For independent events, multiply.

parts.prompt: Find the median of 9, 3, 7, 12, 4, 10.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates must put the values in order first. With an even number of values, the median is halfway between the middle two.

parts.prompt: Simplify √75 + √12.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates wrote √87, incorrectly adding the numbers under the root signs.

parts.prompt: y is directly proportional to the square of x. When x = {a}, y = {=k*a^2}. Find y when x = {b}.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used y = kx, ignoring 'the square of'.

parts.prompt: Write the recurring decimal 0.454545… as a fraction in its simplest form.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates gave 45/99 without simplifying, losing the final mark.

parts.prompt: Factorise x² − 5x − 14.

markingPoints.text: or B1 for factors giving two correct terms when expanded

parts.examinerComment: Sign errors were common, such as (x + 7)(x − 2). Expanding to check is quick.

parts.prompt: f(x) = {a}x − {b} and g(x) = x² + {c}. Find fg({k}).
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates applied f first. In fg(x), g is applied first.

parts.prompt: f(x) = (x + {b})/{a}. Find f⁻¹({k}).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates calculated f({k}) instead of the inverse.

parts.prompt: y = {a}x³ − {b}x. Find the gradient of the curve when x = {k}.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates substituted into y instead of dy/dx.

parts.prompt: Simplify (2x³y)⁴.

markingPoints.text: or B1 for two of 16, x¹², y⁴ in a product

parts.examinerComment: A frequent error was 8x¹²y⁴, multiplying 2 by 4 instead of raising it to the power 4.

parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line that is perpendicular to y = 2x + 1 and passes through (4, 3). Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates knew that the product of perpendicular gradients is −1. Some used ½ instead of −½.

parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the line {a}x + {b}y = {c}.

markingPoints.text: M1 for rearranging to y = {=-a/b}x + {=c/b} or equivalent

parts.examinerComment: A common error was {a}/{b}, ignoring the sign change when rearranging.

parts.prompt: A is ({x1}, {y1}) and B is ({=x1+d}, {=y1+m*d}). Find the gradient of a line perpendicular to AB.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates stopped after finding the gradient of AB.

parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line through (−1, 4) and (3, −4). Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.
parts.examinerComment: Errors with negative coordinates were common, particularly 3 − (−1).

parts.prompt: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle ABC = 104°. Find angle ADC. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.

markingPoints.text: B1 for opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°

parts.examinerComment: Reasons must use correct geometrical language. 'Opposite angles are equal' is a property of parallelograms, not cyclic quadrilaterals.

parts.prompt: PT is a tangent to a circle with centre O, touching the circle at T. Angle TOP = 58°. Find angle OPT. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.

markingPoints.text: B1 for the tangent is perpendicular to the radius (angle OTP = 90°)

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found 32°. The reason needs to mention both the tangent and the radius.

parts.prompt: The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is {=(n-2)*180}°. Find the number of sides of the polygon.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates divided by 180 and forgot to add 2.

parts.prompt: A, B and C are points on a circle. The tangent to the circle at A makes an angle of 47° with the chord AB. C lies on the major arc AB. Find angle ACB. Give a geometrical reason for your answer.

markingPoints.text: B1 for the alternate segment theorem

parts.examinerComment: Few candidates named the alternate segment theorem. Learn the names of the circle theorems.

parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius {r} cm and angle 90°. Find the area of the sector as a multiple of π. Enter the multiple only (for 10π enter 10).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found the arc length instead of the area.

parts.prompt: Solve sin x = 0.5 for 90° < x < 180°.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates gave 30°, which is outside the given range. Use the symmetry of the sine graph about x = 90°.

parts.prompt: O is the origin, OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB. Find OM in terms of a and b, in its simplest form.

markingPoints.text: M1 for AB = b − a or a correct route OA + ½AB

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates wrote AB = a − b, reversing the direction.

parts.prompt: Triangle P has vertices (2, 2), (4, 2) and (2, 6). Triangle Q has vertices (1, 1), (2, 1) and (1, 3). Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle P onto triangle Q.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates gave a scale factor of 2, mixing up the object and the image.

parts.prompt: The point (5, −2) is reflected in the line y = x. Write down the coordinates of its image.
parts.examinerComment: Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates.

parts.prompt: A is the point (2, −3) and B is the point (7, 1). Find the vector AB, giving your answer as (x, y).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found the vector BA, (−5, −4), by subtracting the wrong way round.

parts.prompt: Triangle T has vertices (2, 3), (4, 3) and (2, 4). Triangle U has vertices (0, 1), (−2, 1) and (0, 0). Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle T onto triangle U.
parts.examinerComment: Finding the midpoint of each object point and its image locates the centre of a 180° rotation.

parts.prompt: In a class of 30 students, 18 study French, 14 study Spanish and 5 study neither. A student is chosen at random. Find the probability that the student studies both French and Spanish. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: A Venn diagram helps. Some candidates forgot to include the 5 students who study neither.

parts.prompt: The mean of six numbers is {m}. One number is removed and the mean of the remaining five numbers is {=m-d}. Find the number that was removed.
parts.examinerComment: Working with totals rather than means is the key step.

parts.prompt: A cumulative frequency table shows: time ≤ 10 minutes: 8 people; ≤ 20: 23; ≤ 30: 41; ≤ 40: 50. Find how many people took more than 20 minutes.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates gave 41 − 23 = 18, the number in the 20 to 30 minute class only.

parts.prompt:
A scatter diagram shows the daily temperature and the number of hot drinks sold at a café. As the temperature increases, the number of hot drinks sold decreases.
(i) Write down the type of correlation.
(ii) Explain why a line of best fit should not be used to estimate sales on a day when the temperature is much higher than any in the data.

markingPoints.text: B1 for it would be extrapolation / outside the range of the data, so the trend may not continue

parts.examinerComment: Most identified negative correlation. Stronger answers used the word extrapolation in part (ii).

parts.prompt: The price of a jacket is ${P}. The price is increased by {r}%. Find the new price, in dollars.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found the increase, ${=P*r/100}, but did not add it to the original price.

parts.prompt: Ravi invests ${P} at {r}% per year simple interest. Calculate the total interest he receives after {n} years, in dollars.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates gave the total value of the investment, ${=P+P*r*n/100}, instead of the interest.

parts.prompt: In a sale, all prices are reduced by {r}%. A coat costs ${=O*(1-r/100)} in the sale. Find the price of the coat before the sale, in dollars.
parts.examinerComment: The most common error was to increase the sale price by {r}%, giving {=O*(1-r/100)*(1+r/100)}.

parts.prompt: A car travels {d} km in {t} hours. Calculate its average speed, in km/h.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. A few candidates multiplied distance by time.

parts.prompt: v = u + at. Find v when u = {u}, a = {a} and t = {t}.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates substituted correctly. Some added {u} and {a} before multiplying by {t}.

parts.prompt: Make r the subject of the formula C = 2πr.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates wrote r = C − 2π, subtracting instead of dividing.

parts.prompt: Find the length of the line segment joining ({x1}, {y1}) and ({=x1+dx}, {=y1+dy}). Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: A sketch of the right-angled triangle formed by the two points helped many candidates.

parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line that is parallel to y = 3x − 1 and passes through (0, 4).
parts.examinerComment: Parallel lines have the same gradient. Some candidates used −1 as the gradient.

parts.prompt: A regular polygon has {n} sides. Calculate the size of each interior angle, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates gave the exterior angle, {=360/n}°, as their final answer.

parts.prompt: Triangles ABC and PQR are similar. AB = {a} cm, PQ = {=a*k} cm and BC = {b} cm. Find QR, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates added the difference in lengths instead of multiplying by the scale factor.

parts.prompt: Calculate the area of a circle of radius {r} cm, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used 2πr, which gives the circumference.

parts.prompt: A cylinder has radius {r} cm and height {h} cm. Calculate its volume, in cm³.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Convert {a} m² into cm².
parts.examinerComment: The most common error was multiplying by 100 instead of 100² = 10 000.

parts.prompt: In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite angle x is {o} cm and the side adjacent to angle x is {a} cm. Calculate x, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who labelled the sides first usually chose the correct ratio.

parts.prompt: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse {=a+d} cm and one of the shorter sides {a} cm. Calculate the length of the third side, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates added the squares instead of subtracting. The hypotenuse is always the longest side.

parts.prompt: A ladder of length {L} m leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is on horizontal ground, {d} m from the wall. Calculate the angle between the ladder and the ground, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used sin instead of cos and found the angle between the ladder and the wall.

parts.prompt: From a point on level ground {d} m from the foot of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is {t}°. Calculate the height of the tower, in m.
parts.examinerComment: Check that your calculator is in degree mode. Answers from radian mode were seen.

parts.prompt: A shape is enlarged. A side of length {a} cm becomes a side of length {=a*k} cm. Find the scale factor of the enlargement.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates subtracted the lengths. The scale factor is image length ÷ object length.

parts.prompt: A dice is thrown {n} times. It shows a six {k} times. Find the relative frequency of throwing a six. Give your answer as a decimal correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates gave 1/6, which is the theoretical probability for a fair dice.

parts.prompt: The probability that a light bulb is faulty is {p}. Find the expected number of faulty bulbs in a batch of {n}.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: A bag contains {r} red, {b} blue and {g} green counters. A counter is taken at random. Find the probability that it is not blue. Give your answer as a decimal correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found the probability of blue and did not subtract from 1.

parts.prompt: A frequency table shows scores of 1, 2, 3 and 4 with frequencies {a}, {b}, {c} and {d} respectively. Calculate the mean score.
parts.examinerComment: Dividing by 4, the number of different scores, was a common error.

parts.prompt: In a survey, {k} out of {n} people chose tea as their favourite drink. The results are shown in a pie chart. Calculate the sector angle for tea, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: A car is bought for ${P}. Its value depreciates by {r}% each year. Calculate its value after {n} years, correct to the nearest dollar.
parts.examinerComment: Using a multiplier of 1.{r} instead of {=1-r/100} was a common error.

parts.prompt: The length and width of a rectangle are {L} cm and {W} cm, each correct to the nearest centimetre. Calculate the upper bound of the area, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates calculated the area first and then added 0.5.

parts.prompt: Solve {a}x² + {b}x − {c} = 0, giving the positive solution correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.examinerComment: Sign errors with −4ac when c is negative were common. Write down the values of a, b and c before substituting.

parts.prompt: The lines y = {m}x + {c} and y = {n} − x intersect at P. Find the x-coordinate of P.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates equated the expressions. Errors came from moving terms across the equals sign.

parts.prompt: Two triangles are similar. Corresponding sides have lengths {a} cm and {b} cm. The area of the smaller triangle is {A} cm². Calculate the area of the larger triangle, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Using the length scale factor without squaring was the most common error.

parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius {r} cm and angle {t}°. Calculate the area of the sector, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: A solid hemisphere has radius {r} cm. Calculate its total surface area, including the flat face, in cm².

markingPoints.text: M1 for curved surface ½ × 4 × π × {r}²

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates omitted the circular flat face.

parts.prompt: A cone has base radius {r} cm and perpendicular height {h} cm. Calculate its curved surface area, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Using the perpendicular height instead of the slant height was a common error.

parts.prompt: A cylinder of radius {=r+d} cm contains water. A solid metal sphere of radius {r} cm is placed in the water and is completely covered. Calculate the rise in the water level, in cm.

markingPoints.text: M1 for volume of sphere (4/3) × π × {r}³

parts.examinerComment: Equating the volume of the sphere with the volume of water displaced is the key idea.

parts.prompt: In triangle ABC, angle A = {A}°, angle B = {B}° and BC = {a} cm. Calculate AC, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who labelled sides with the opposite angles' letters made fewer errors pairing them up.

parts.prompt: In triangle PQR, PQ = {c} cm, QR = {a} cm and PR = {b} cm. Calculate angle PRQ, in degrees.
parts.examinerComment: The angle must be opposite the side that appears with the minus sign. Some used the wrong side.

parts.prompt: A cuboid measures {l} cm by {w} cm by {h} cm. Calculate the length of a diagonal joining opposite corners of the cuboid, in cm.

markingPoints.text: M1 for adding {h}² and taking the square root

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found only the diagonal of the base.

parts.prompt: A cuboid measures {l} cm by {w} cm by {h} cm. Calculate the angle between a diagonal of the cuboid and its base, in degrees.

markingPoints.text: M1 for tan θ = {h} ÷ their base diagonal

parts.examinerComment: Identifying the right-angled triangle containing the required angle is the key step. A sketch helps.

parts.prompt: A ship sails {a} km on a bearing of 040° and then {b} km on a bearing of 130°. Calculate its distance from the starting point, in km.

markingPoints.text: B1 for recognising the angle between the two legs is 90°

parts.examinerComment: A sketch with north lines shows the right angle. Some candidates used the cosine rule with an incorrect angle.

parts.prompt: p = ({x}, −{y}) as a column vector. Calculate |p|, in its simplest form or correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates subtracted the squares because of the negative component.

parts.prompt: a = ({p}, {q}) and b = ({r}, −{s}) as column vectors. Calculate |a − b|, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Errors in subtracting a negative component were common.

parts.prompt: The probability that it rains on a given day is {p}. If it rains, the probability that Ana is late is {a}. If it does not rain, the probability that she is late is {b}. Find the probability that Ana is late.
parts.examinerComment: A tree diagram helps. Many candidates found only one of the two branches.

parts.prompt: The probability that it rains on a given day is {p}. If it rains, the probability that Ana is late is {a}. If it does not rain, the probability that she is late is {b}. Given that Ana is late, find the probability that it rained.
parts.examinerComment: Stronger candidates recognised the conditional probability and divided by P(late). Many simply gave {=p*a}.

parts.prompt: A box contains {r} red pens and {b} blue pens. Two pens are taken at random without replacement. Find the probability that both are blue. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates forgot that there are fewer pens for the second pick.

parts.prompt: A fair six-sided dice is thrown {n} times. Find the probability of getting at least one six. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Using 1 − P(no sixes) is much quicker than listing all the cases.

parts.prompt: On a histogram, the class 10 < t ≤ 25 has a frequency density of {d}. Find the frequency of this class.
parts.examinerComment: Frequency = frequency density × class width. Some candidates used 25 as the class width.

parts.prompt: A group of {n1} students has a mean mark of {m1}. Another group of {n2} students has a mean mark of {m2}. Calculate the mean mark of all {=n1+n2} students.
parts.examinerComment: Averaging the two means, giving {=(m1+m2)/2}, ignores the different group sizes.

parts.prompt: On a histogram, the class 20 < m ≤ 50 has frequency {f}. Calculate the frequency density of this class.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates divided by the upper class boundary, 50, instead of the class width.
